transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
U.S. military says it has disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman.
As it has attempted to break the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports,
the strike comes as the Trump administration has been non-committal on its next moves
nine months into the war against Iran.
And PR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
U.S. Central Command says a military aircraft fired "precision munitions"
at a merchant vessel attempting to leave an Iranian port.
CENTCOM said in a statement that the civilian crew of the ship was "unharmed."
The U.S. military has been blocking Iranian ports since April.
It temporarily lifted the blockade over the summer during talks with Tehran,
but resumed it in July.
This strike was the 15th ship the U.S. has disclosed disabling during its blockade,
including at least two strikes that have resulted in the killing of multiple crew members.
President Trump has wavered on what to do next in Iran,
suggesting on Thanksgiving Day that the end of the war will be "whenever he decides."
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
Stocks rose as this holiday shortened week-ended early.
These gains are welcomed by investors who have spent the past several days worrying about AI.
NPR's Maham Javed reports.
After several days of volatile fluctuations, mostly due to tech indexes,
U.S. stocks posted strong returns this week before the market closed today.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.6 percent with broad gains.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2 percent.
And the tech-heavy NASDAQ Composite rose 2.3 percent.
The biggest jump this week was on Monday when Jensen Huang, the CEO of NVIDIA,
was reinstated as the head of the semiconductor company.
Those gains have held despite big ups and downs on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Semiconductor stocks bounced back as investors relaxed about instability in the AI market.
The market was shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday and closed early for Black Friday.
Maham Javed, NPR News.
Political opposition leaders in Israel are progressing in forming a new government
and unseating Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports.
And Netanyahu is not likely to take this lightly.
We may see Netanyahu make attempts to undermine this emerging government,
this very ideologically diverse coalition.
He may try to bring down that new government and trigger new elections.
And that's why we're seeing the opposition worried now.
And they're trying to rush to declare a government as early as next week.
They're worried Netanyahu could launch even a war against Iran in the coming days.
And it would complicate their attempt to get him out of power.
The opposition is led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot,
who has the support of the majority of the newly elected parliament in Israel.
Eisenkot has until December 6th to form a governing coalition.
You're listening to NPR.
There are big crowds at the movie theaters this weekend,
as NPR's Bob Mondello reports.
Hollywood is optimistic about an end-of-the-year box office bonanza.
With a Hunger Games sequel.
Twice the number of tributes, twice the glory.
Helping to push this weekend's ticket sales above $200 million,
movie theater owners are turning their attention to next month,
and what's likely to be the biggest sequel-driven opening day in Hollywood history.
December 18, when the conclusion of Denis Villeneuve's Dune trilogy
opened on the same day as Marvel's superhero epic Avengers Doomsday.
I am Dune.
Fans are calling the blockbuster battle Dune's Day,
and they've already ponied up tens of millions of dollars
for advanced tickets to both films.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
President Trump plans to visit Arizona next week,
where he'll speak at the groundbreaking of a new computer chip foundry
for a Taiwan semiconductor manufacturing company.
That company has been expanding in the Phoenix area,
manufacturing chips for major tech companies, including Nvidia.
The President's trip comes after he intervened
to get his friend Jensen Wong reinstated as the CEO of Nvidia.
Wong will be testifying before Congress next week,
and he will be facing numerous questions,
both in open session and in closed-door testimony,
about multiple affairs that briefly cost him his job.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: U.S. military disables a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman attempting to break the Iranian port blockade
U.S. stocks rise for the holiday-shortened week, with gains led by tech indexes after Jensen Huang's reinstatement
Israeli opposition leaders, led by Gadi Eisenkot, move to form a government and unseat Netanyahu
Big weekend movie box office crowds, with Hunger Games sequel pushing ticket sales above $200 million
Trump plans Arizona visit to speak at groundbreaking of Taiwan Semiconductor chip foundry in Phoenix area
Jensen Huang to testify before Congress next week about affairs that briefly cost him Nvidia's top job
